newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Barley Board boosts feed pool.
newsitem.headline: Australian Barley Board boosts feed pool.

text.p: The Australian Barley Board (ABB) has increased its 1996/97 feed barley pool price by A$5.00 to A$162.00 a tonne.
The malting barley pool price is unchanged at A$210.00 a tonne.

ABB chief executive officer Michael Iwaniw said the higher pool price resulted from cash flow from an early shipping programme, and a very strong feed sales programme last season with some markets requiring immediate shipment of large tonnages as soon as the grain was harvested.
The exchange rate also had been favourable since January.
Almost 60 percent of ABB's export shipping had now occurred, with delivery to domestic customers also strong because of the dry autumn, he said.
Dairy industry demand had been sustained and with the weather outlook suggesting a dry season or worse, demand for stock feed was expected to continue, he said.
Malting barley demand had been more closely matched with available supply, with the market very quiet over the last couple of months, he said.
"It has been a difficult season for maltsters, with reports of considerable stocks of processed malt around the world," he said.
Heavy subsidies on malt exports from Europe capped any chance for malting barley prices to increase, he said.
Malsters said the gap between the price achievable for processed malt and what malsters were paying to obtain malted barley had narrowed significantly, he said.
